messages.subject: reshape2 and aggregation function
parts:
Hi all,

I’m working through Matthew Jockers’ Text Analysis with R for Students of Literature and while Jockers words largely with list objects, I like to get things into a data frame as quickly as possible. I’ve gotten the word frequency data for Moby Dick into a nice data frame, but I’m getting odd error from reshape2 when I want to create a document terms matrix. If I run the code below without specifying an aggregation function I get the error: "Aggregation function missing: defaulting to length"

rm(list=ls())
library(reshape2)
chapter.df <- read.table("http://www.history.emory.edu/RAVINA/Moby.txt", header=TRUE, stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
chapter.term.matrix <- dcast(chapter.df, Chapter.Nos ~ Words, value.var="Rel.Freq", fill=0)
cor(chapter.term.matrix$ahab, chapter.term.matrix$whale)

The mystery is that since I have only one observation per cell I’m not aggregating

If I add the function mean (see below) the data frame casts perfectly and gets the right results. In fact I get the same correlation coefs if I add the functions mean, min, or max, which suggests that the aggregation function is doing anything, at least not for the cells I’m checking. What’s going on?

rm(list=ls())
library(reshape2)
chapter.df <- read.table("http://www.history.emory.edu/RAVINA/Moby.txt", header=TRUE, stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
chapter.term.matrix <- dcast(chapter.df, Chapter.Nos ~ Words, value.var="Rel.Freq", mean, fill=0)
cor(chapter.term.matrix$ahab, chapter.term.matrix$whale)
chapter.term.matrix <- dcast(chapter.df, Chapter.Nos ~ Words, value.var="Rel.Freq", min, fill=0)
cor(chapter.term.matrix$ahab, chapter.term.matrix$whale)

Mark Ravina
Professor of History
Emory University
Editorial Board, Journal of Asian Studies

Hi Brandon,

Thanks for introducing me to tidyr. With the tidyr error message I found a regex error: I hadn’t considered numbers as words, so I was introducing NA’s.  Fixed the regex and fixed the problem.

Thanks again,
Mark
